problem: A particle accelerates from rest with a constant acceleration of $1\,{\text{km/h}}^{2}$ for the first $3$ hours of its motion. It then travels at a constant speed for the next $3$ hours before accelerating with a constant acceleration of $0.5\,{\text{km/h}}^{2}$ for other $3$ hours. Which graph represents the described motion?

feedback.problem: A train accelerates from rest with a constant acceleration of $3\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}$ for the first $10$ seconds of its motion. Then the train decelerates with a constant deceleration of $1\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}$ for the next $15$ seconds, before traveling at a constant speed for the next $20$ seconds. Which graph represents the described motion?
feedback.worked_solution:
We start the first line from the point $(0,0),$ since the train starts from rest. Then, because the acceleration is $3\,{\text{m/s}}^{2},$ we draw a line with slope $3.$ 

However, because the train is only accelerating for the first $10$ seconds, we stop the line at $t=10.$ At this time, the train's speed has increased by $10\cdot 3=30\text{ m/s}.$ So, the first line segment goes from $(0,0)$ to $(10,30).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13945962/assets/54ac34c5fe7833d42fb8ddda729d3823ff0e726e1e6228492639a9e91bad2762.png)

After $t=10$, the train has a deceleration of $1\,{\text{m/s}}^{2},$ so the slope of the second line segment is $-1.$ The second line segment stops after $15$ seconds. To figure out the velocity at this moment, we need to find the equation for the second line segment.

Since the second line segment passes through the point $(10,30)$ and has a slope of $-1,$ we can use point-slope form to write the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}v-{v}_{1} & =m(t-{t}_{1}) \\ v-30 & =-(t-10) \\ v-30 & =-t+10 \\ v & =-t+40\end{aligned}
$$

The second line segment stops when $t=10+15=25$ seconds, and the velocity at this moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =-t+40 \\ v & =-25+40 \\ v & =15\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13945962/assets/b199170cfdadd688a15668afdbac796a90fc158c94bfc0ffc8b9245c5a741e8e.png)

The train then travels at a constant speed for the next $20$ seconds. So, the speed remains at $15\,\text{m/s}$ for the next $20$ seconds, until $t=25+20=45.$

Finally, the third line segment stops at the point $(45,15).$ The final graph is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13945962/assets/b1ece8dd03146aaf420746b6ba3cc59b3d707150fe3682bbdcd6f05d645fb4c4.png)
